text: The Studienstiftung des deutschen Volkes is a German scholarship foundation established in 1925, dissolved in 1934, and re-founded in 1948. It offers scholarships to undergraduate and graduate students, including PhD candidates, based on academic excellence, initiative, and responsibility. Scholarships are awarded through multiple pathways: nomination by high schools, professors, or examination boards; participation in national or international competitions; self-identification via an assessment test; nomination by alumni; or support for students in the arts. Financial support includes a monthly allowance (€300), need-based subsidies (up to €855/month), and partial tuition coverage, with tax-free payments under German income tax law. Additional academic support includes summer academies, workshops, mentoring, and research opportunities. As of 2023, 71.5% of scholars received the basic allowance, 16.4% a partial need-based scholarship, and 11.1% the maximum need-based scholarship. Scholarships are renewable for up to five years based on academic performance and engagement. The foundation also supports doctoral candidates with a monthly award of €1,550 (increasing to €1,650 from 2025) and research allowances. The organization emphasizes both financial and academic development, with a focus on fostering excellence and social responsibility.
